Definition: Integration of company registration, business licensing, tax compliance, regulatory compliance data
Comments: No evidence of business registration integration with a data exchange platform found. Digital services fragmentation is well-documented.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original source was a general e-government barriers paper providing no domain-specific evidence. Fresh search found concrete, dated evidence of business-registration integration efforts: (i) an April 2026 GIA/Union of Chambers of Commerce meeting to launch an electronic Chambers system explicitly designed for 'interoperability with national platforms, foremost among them the National Data Distributor (LY-NDEX)'; (ii) a February 2026 reactivation of the Commercial Registry Authority's One-Stop Shop, reviewing 'potential integration with the Authority's digital infrastructure'; (iii) an ongoing EU-funded eRegulations/eJraat business-registration digitisation project. These show active, dated work-in-progress but no confirmed operational integration yet, so the score is revised upward from Unknown to 'Under development' (3), not higher.
revised_comments: Business registration and licensing integration with the government data exchange is under active development. In April 2026 the General Information Authority and the Union of Chambers of Commerce agreed to build an electronic Chambers system designed for interoperability with the National Data Distributor (LY-NDEX), and in February 2026 the Commercial Registry Authority began reactivating its One-Stop Shop for company registration, reviewing integration with its digital infrastructure. An EU-funded eRegulations/eJraat platform (UNCTAD, Expertise France) also supports digitisation of business-registration procedures. None of these initiatives is yet confirmed as fully operational or integrated.

Definition: Integration of CRVS data (births, deaths, marriages) into data exchange for real-time verification and service eligibility
Comments: Libya's fragmented governance and post-conflict context has prevented coherent digital systems development.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original single source was general background only. Found the Civil Registration Authority's 'Intilaqa' project (ongoing since 2022, reported September 2024), which reconciles paper and electronic civil-registry records and underpins the National ID Number used across passports, SIM registration, banking and voting — but this is a data-cleaning exercise, not documented evidence that CRVS data itself is fed into the GIA's National Data Distributor (LY-NDEX) for real-time cross-agency verification. Because the CRA's National Number is foundational to many other systems there is a plausible case for at least partial integration, but no source confirms this explicitly for CRVS records. Flagged for human review rather than guessing a score; original Unknown (0) retained pending confirmation.
revised_comments: The Civil Registration Authority has been reconciling paper and electronic vital-records data through its 'Intilaqa' project since 2022, and CRA data underlies the National ID Number used across government services. However, no publicly available source confirms that civil registration and vital statistics data are formally integrated into the national government data exchange for real-time verification or service eligibility.

Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: Libya lacks laws recognizing electronic transactions and digital identities broadly according to academic research. Political instability has impeded coherent digital ID development.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original sources (Shwehdy 2025 conference paper and blog post) predate or do not reference Libya's National Digital Identity System (LY-DNID) and understate the true status. Found that Level 1 of LY-DNID already enables government-to-government (G2G) electronic communication and has been adopted by 'a number of institutions and public entities' (GIA, 20 Nov 2025). A Level 2 pilot for citizen-facing authentication launched November 2025, with direct integration with the National Data Distributor (LY-NDEX). A Level 3 (biometric) is in technical trials with the Central Bank of Libya for eKYC/banking services (April 2026), not yet in full production. This constitutes partial, multi-agency integration, so the score is revised from Unknown (0) to 'Partially integrated' (4); it falls short of 'Fully Integrated' (5) since citizen-facing rollout and full banking integration remain in pilot/trial stages.
revised_comments: Libya's National Digital Identity System (LY-DNID) is partially integrated with the government data exchange. Its first level already supports government-to-government electronic authentication and has been adopted by a number of public institutions, directly linked to the National Data Distributor (LY-NDEX). A second level, aimed at citizen-facing authentication, entered pilot operation in November 2025, and a biometric third level is undergoing technical trials with the Central Bank of Libya and participating banks for identity verification (eKYC) in financial services as of April 2026. Full nationwide, cross-sector rollout is not yet complete.

Definition: Integration of tax administration and revenue collection systems data into the exchange platform
Comments: No evidence of tax/revenue system integration with a data exchange platform found. The GIA's digital transformation efforts do not reference tax integration.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original source stated the GIA's digital transformation efforts do not reference tax integration; fresh search found this has moved on. The Libyan Tax Authority operates an electronic tax portal (ly.tax) integrated with electronic payment services, formalised by Decision No. 247/2024 permitting electronic income-tax collection, and the Central Bank of Libya is rolling out POS-based e-collection for the Tax Authority, Customs Authority and Ports Company from May 2026. However, a 2024 peer-reviewed study of the Libyan Tax Authority found that 'coordination between the Tax Authority and other relevant entities (such as customs, banks, and the commercial registry) remains limited in effectiveness,' indicating cross-agency data exchange is still nascent rather than operational. Score revised from Unknown (0) to 'Under development' (3).
revised_comments: Libya's Tax Authority has digitised core functions through an electronic tax portal (ly.tax) integrated with electronic payment services, underpinned by a 2024 ministerial decision permitting electronic income-tax collection, and the Central Bank of Libya began rolling out point-of-sale electronic collection for tax, customs and port revenues in May 2026. A 2024 academic study of the Tax Authority found that coordination and data-sharing with other agencies, including customs, banks and the commercial registry, remains limited in effectiveness, indicating that broader cross-government data-exchange integration is still under development rather than operational.

revised_comments: Libya approved a draft Unified Social Registry in June 2025, intended to integrate citizens' social and economic data across social-assistance programmes into a single database with periodic updates, addressing a previously fragmented landscape in which the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Social Solidarity Fund lacked a shared beneficiary registry. As of the latest available evidence the registry remains under development rather than operational.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: The GIA publishes limited information on digital transformation activities. The LY-GOVREP platform is described as a transparency tool. The UNDP-GIA MoU has been publicly announced. However, no public dashboard for data exchange operations and limited disclosure overall.
redteam_note: Value Name differs from the scale label — usually cosmetic.
revision_notes: Original sources (LY-GOVREP launch, UNDP MoU) supported only 'Low - Limited Disclosure.' Fresh search found that the GIA launched a public Open Government Data Platform (opendata.gia.gov.ly) in November 2025, publishing a national open-data policy and technical (Standard & Metadata) guide, and by February 2026 had published 91 datasets from 9 government entities across 8 sectors, with APIs for automated reuse, and stated plans to link the platform to the National Data Distributor (LY-NDEX). The GIA also routinely publishes detailed, dated updates on specific data-governance and interoperability projects (e.g. Zakat Fund, Chambers of Commerce, digital-identity roll-out). This constitutes a public platform with regularly published datasets and reports, going beyond 'limited disclosure' though it does not yet amount to a dedicated public dashboard specifically for data-exchange operations and data-sharing agreements. Score revised from 'Low - Limited Disclosure' (2) to 'Moderate = Annual Reports' (3).
revised_comments: The General Information Authority publishes a growing body of information on government data governance and exchange activity. Its Open Government Data Platform (opendata.gia.gov.ly), launched in November 2025, had published 91 datasets from nine government entities across eight sectors by February 2026, alongside a national open-data policy and technical standards guide, and is intended to be linked to the National Data Distributor (LY-NDEX). The Authority also regularly publishes dated updates on specific interoperability and data-governance initiatives. This amounts to moderate, periodic public disclosure, though a dedicated public dashboard specifically covering data-exchange governance and data-sharing agreements has not yet been established.
